verdict.rationale: Alma's O-1A founders guide says a company you own or founded can petition for you if a valid employer-employee relationship exists. It also covers control arrangements: solo founders without an independent board can use a U.S. Agent as petitioner, and proper entity structuring helps avoid ownership-control RFEs. Missing for 10: explicit beneficial-ownership rules, detailed board-control mechanics, any reference to the 2023+ USCIS founder guidance, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the provider documents how my own startup can petition for me — beneficial-ownership rules, board or employer control arrangements, and the 2023+ USCIS founder guidance

citations.quote: a U.S. company you own or founded can file an O-1A petition on your behalf, provided you establish a valid employer-employee relationship.

For solo founders without an independent board, or founders operating across multiple entities, an authorized U.S. Agent can serve as the legal petitioner. Proper entity structuring from the outset prevents Requests for Evidence (RFEs) challenging ownership control.
